about: Fork addition (plan 40): settings Cosmos proposes for images whose own declaration is not enough. Data, not code: read by src/anyimage/recipes.go, checked by recipes_test.go and, against the real images, by recipes_live_test.go. Each recipe cites the image's documentation in 'source'. 'maintained': when the image was last published, as read on the day 'checked' (an unmaintained image gets no recipe: MinIO's community image is gone and its repository archived since April 2026); the exception is an image that people still run, frozen by its publisher, whose recipe carries a note ending in 'Frozen' saying so: Bitnami's legacy catalogue, Redis Stack). 'family': the id of the recipe for the same software from its main publisher (other publishers' images, with their own variables, folders or tags); the panel recognises such a database among the containers but does not offer it as a new one. 'pin', 'prefer' and 'tagSuffix' follow the publisher's tags: no 'pin' where only 'latest' is published (bitnami, bitnamisecure, Chainguard's free images), 'prefer' a tag that names the major where the version tags do not (pgvector's pg18). Volume 'evidence': declared (the image declares this VOLUME), workdir (its WORKDIR), env:NAME (a variable of the image points there or below), docs (only the documentation says so). 'runAs': the uid:gid the container runs as (first entry whose tagContains is in the tag), so that Cosmos makes the data folder its own; the live test checks the image's user has that id. A port marked 'undeclared' is opened by the recipe's command, not by the image. Env 'type': secret (a strong random value, generated in the browser), name (a value to choose, proposed), optional (shown folded, empty unless set), fixed (set as given). 'login' (plan 45): how one signs in to the image and what its sign-in details must be: 'where' (database, web, s3, amqp, http; 'via': database for a tool one signs in to with the database's own accounts), 'accounts' (the variables holding each account's user or e-mail, password and database; 'userFixed' a user the image fixes, 'userUnset' the user when the variable is not set; 'defaults' marks the one account that takes the configured default username and e-mail), 'user' (a pattern Go and JavaScript read alike, the maximum length, reserved names), 'email' (refuseSpecialUse: .local, .test and the like are refused), 'password' (min, max at most 64, the symbols allowed besides letters and digits, a subset of the URL-unreserved -._~, the classes required); every rule cites its 'evidence', and the live test signs in with a generated password holding every class allowed. 'manager': a web tool that manages databases of these kinds ('for'), the lowest 'rank' proposed first; its 'needs.env' maps host, port, user, password, database or url to its variables, 'needs.servers' and 'needs.passFile' name the variables that carry pgAdmin's server list and password file. 'entrypoint': replaces the image's entrypoint (exec form); used only for a small sh wrapper that writes such a variable into the tool's own volume (umask 077) and then execs the image's own entrypoint; the script holds no value. 'firstRun': apps that create their first account in their own page at first open (note firstRunPage) or print a temporary password in their log for a fixed user (note logPassword), so Cosmos cannot set it and only proposes what to type there; each cites its documentation.

entrypoint: d=/var/lib/pgadmin/cosmos; (umask 077; mkdir -p "$d" || exit 1; if [ -n "$PGADMIN_COSMOS_SERVERS" ]; then printf '%s' "$PGADMIN_COSMOS_SERVERS" > "$d/servers.json" || exit 1; fi; if [ -n "$PGADMIN_COSMOS_PGPASS" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$PGADMIN_COSMOS_PGPASS" > "$d/pgpass" || exit 1; fi) || exit 1; unset PGADMIN_COSMOS_SERVERS PGADMIN_COSMOS_PGPASS; exec /entrypoint.sh "$@"
